cost_report.environment: AWS account, whole project (Cost Explorer, credits excluded)
cost_report.gap: The bill is a whole-day, whole-account figure. The ECS/ALB share of the 2026-11-18 load, the cost of one request and the cost per 1,000 requests are GAPS: no per-service, per-hour or per-resource cost export was saved before the stack was destroyed, so the load's own cost cannot be separated from Neptune, EMR and the rest of the day.

elasticity_aws_ecs.column_meaning: desired running pending (ECS service counts; the decision log reads the 20:52:55Z line as desired 2 running 1 pending 1)
elasticity_aws_ecs.configured_cooldown_note: Scale-in cooldown 300 s and scale-out cooldown 60 s are the configured values in the Terraform policy, recorded in docs/agent-runs/phase-15/owner-report.md (the P41 section, 'Cooldowns: scale-in 300, scale-out 60'); they are configuration, not a measurement.

dashboard_reading.source: docs/agent-runs/phase-15/evidence/session-2/00-timeline/decision-log.md:65 (human reading of the dashboard clip; not a raw export)

scale_in.interpretation_limit: The desired count fell somewhere inside this bracket (the polls in between are blank); the exact scale-in instant is a GAP. The decision log records a dashboard reading of about 21:09-21:10Z (human-read from a clip, not a raw export).

scale_out.interpretation_limit: The polls before the last_poll_with_data_before line are blank, so the instant the desired count changed is unknown; the figures above are upper bounds measured from the poll grid (about 61 s). No CloudWatch alarm history or ECS service-event export was saved: the exact scale-out trigger delay is a GAP.

elasticity_aws_ecs.source: docs/agent-runs/phase-15/evidence/session-2/b10-load/b10-ecs-poll.log (committed evidence copy; polls were taken by a human-run loop, not a CloudWatch export)

emr_cost.note: The first record (window end 16:56:18Z) is superseded by the second (cluster end 17:06:31Z); the billed window includes idle time after the failed Spark step.

emr_steps.interpretation_limit: Only submission instants are logged (the step runtime is not read from the EMR console), so a step time is the gap to the next submission or to the failure line: an upper bound that includes the poll interval and one pre-spend receipt check. The Spark job failed with 'Unknown Error.' (s1-spark-failure.json), so EMR has no Spark runtime to report.

emr_vs_local_same_input.interpretation_limit: Descriptive only: one EMR run (2 nodes, the second node r5.xlarge primary) against one laptop run; EMR time includes YARN start-up and S3/EFS staging, the laptop uses local files. No scaling claim (speed-up with node count) can be made: only one cluster size was ever completed.

failure_recovery_aws_ecs.interpretation_limit: Recovery is measured with a probe every ~5 s on the public ALB host (healthz and readyz), so it carries about +/-5 s resolution. Two stop-task calls took effect; the call logged between them was a repeat on an already-stopped task (decision log) and shows no outage. Two events are not a distribution: no percentile is given.

llm_answer_latency.note: Q12 answers include a live Anthropic call and the graph retrieval; the loopback client is the same machine as the service. The probe runs are one answer each. The p50 bootstrap interval resamples these questions only: it describes this question mix (answered, abstained and refused questions together), not a population of questions.

paired_q12.note: The two runs ask the same 33 questions at different commits (ec675d5 and 827fcd5), after planner and service changes: they are different code, not repeats. Run-to-run variability is therefore not measured, and the difference is not a causal estimate.

local_chain.note: Local single-machine runs. Several early runs failed or were diagnostic (all_steps_passed false); they are listed, not hidden. Compare an EMR step with a local step only for the same input (size S = 15a size-100 slice) and at the same commit (bd0b818).

scope: offline recomputation from raw evidence; no network, AWS, model call or spend
threats_to_validity: The P35 raw (83 MB) is not in the repository: a reader without the laptop can check those rows only against the committed harness summary and the raw sha256, not recompute them.
Single runs: each load level was run once; percentiles are point estimates and the per-minute spread is the only variability evidence.
Load generator and service share the laptop in the LOCAL-LOOPBACK rows, and in the Q12 rows the client, the service and the graph export are one machine; those numbers are not AWS numbers.
The AWS run used the semantic route only (no LLM, graph routes dropped), so its throughput does not describe /v1/query.
The aborted AWS run covers about 32 s of hold-50, so the steady-state hold behaviour on AWS is unmeasured.
EMR step times are upper bounds from submission instants, not from the EMR console.
Token costs are the synthesis call only at the pinned rates (estimates); the Anthropic console is the cost of record.
